arguments.text: Good start. Settle now to race rhythm, long way to go.

6000 m, 6 legs of 1000 m out-and-back. Goal fastest finish. Plan: after the hot start, hold shaft power near sustainable_shaft_power (about CP 207 W pod) so the pod reserve lasts; spend a bit more on legs against the current, a bit less with it. Final push from about 400 m out, finish cue at about 250 m. Check CP with heart-rate trend at steady effort (rising HR at steady power = above true CP). Watch for weed (speed drops at same pod power, push_local falls vs push_along), pod drift (pod power changes while GPS speed and HR stay), radio course changes.

Flat HR at 212 W pod suggests pod CP 207 is about right or slightly low. Pod reserve 45%, boat reserve 27% (boat model drains faster; boat CP 119 may be low or current fit off). Leg 1 heads north into current; measure fit says push -0.05 if computer share 0.58 is right, vs push_along -0.13.

arguments.text: t=400s: hull fit legs1-2: share 0.648, current 0.17 m/s against on out legs (north), with on back. HR trend leg1 +0.6+-0.2 bpm/min at pod 213 W: slightly above CP, so pod CP 207 about right. Set boat CP 134 W, boat reserve 9.9 kJ to match. Normal baselines: drag_gap about +0.09 both directions; pod_ratio about 1.55 (1.51 back, 1.59 out). Pod reserve 35% at 400 s; hold about 210 W pod, final push with remaining reserve. Into-current extra effort gains only about 1 s per leg pair: low priority.

t=433s: paddler said cooked, cannot hold; asked: 8/10, really hurting. Instruments: pod 211 W (CP 207), HR flat 174.6-174.9 over last 100 s (rose 2 bpm over 150-330 s), no speed fade, pod reserve 40%. Judged it as normal near-CP discomfort; cued reassure. If HR starts climbing >1 bpm/min or speed fades at same rate, reconsider (CP may be lower).

text: Cued reassure: paddler says cooked (8/10) but HR is flat, speed not fading, pod at CP with 40% reserve.

arguments.text: Yes, speed dropped at same effort. Back-stroke to clear the rudder.

Holding 208-210 W spends the reserve exactly by the finish, so the final sprint must come from saving a little on with-current legs. Paddler tends to sag below CP when not cued; push cues last several minutes.
